raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Updates the requirements on [tensordict](https://github.com/pytorch/tensordict) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from tensordict's releases.

TensorDict v0.15.1

Highlights

TensorDict 0.15.1 is a patch release with 46 bug fixes. They cover update_, copy_ and in-place math on lazy stacks, h5 files and TypedTensorDict, UnbatchedTensor and non-tensor data, NumPy conversion, tensordict.nn, and torch.compile. There are no new features or deprecations. Several fixes change behavior that was previously wrong; see "Behavior changes" below.

Bug Fixes

Construction and conversion

  • td.new_tensor(data) takes a list, tuple, NumPy array or scalar, as torch.Tensor.new_tensor does; before, it raised AttributeError (#2748, fixes #2747).
  • A list of tensors of different shapes in TensorDict(...) or set becomes a NonTensorStack, as with from_dict; before, it raised AttributeError (#2751).
  • NumPy arrays with negative strides, fields of packed structured arrays and big-endian arrays are copied into a tensordict; before, they raised a misleading ValueError (#2853, #2855, fixes #2852, fixes #2854).

Keys, get, set and update

  • td.update({"x": td}), and p["x"] = p on a TensorDictParams, raise ValueError; before, they left a tensordict that holds itself, or raised RecursionError (#2764).
  • Gradients flow through update_ and copy_; before, backward() through the written leaves raised, and compiled code with these calls failed to compile (#2881, fixes #2863, fixes #2886).
  • copy_, update_ (also with keys_to_update) and in-place math write the h5 files and lazy stacks that a TensorDict holds; before, these silently kept their values (#2777, #2838, fixes #2775, fixes #2780).
  • split_keys(..., reproduce_struct=True) puts each non-tensor entry, and each entry that only some lazy-stack members hold, in one part; before, every part got a copy (#2802, #2841, fixes #2782, fixes #2803).

Arithmetic, reductions and torch functions

  • torch.where(mask, 0, td) and torch.where(mask, tensor, td) work on tensordicts and tensorclasses; before, they raised AttributeError and TypeError (#2762, fixes #2743).
  • named_apply(fn, out=buf) writes into buf and returns it, as apply does; before, it returned a new tensordict and left buf unchanged (#2846, fixes #2845).

Lazy stacks, stack and cat

  • Printing a lazy stack or a TypedTensorDict over one stacks no tensors; before, it stacked every entry twice, which can exhaust GPU memory (#2799, #2829, fixes #2783, fixes #2800).
  • filter_empty_() and split_keys() work on a lazy stack whose members hold empty sub-tensordicts; before, they raised KeyError (#2806, fixes #2796).
  • When one member of a lazy stack rejects its part of update_ or copy_, nothing is written; before, the earlier members were already written (#2837, fixes #2776).
  • update_ and copy_ broadcast a 0-d or size-1 value into a lazy stack inside a TensorDict; before, the value was silently dropped (#2850, fixes #2834).
  • empty(recurse=True) drops the tensors of a lazy stack inside a tensordict, as at the root; before, member-only tensors kept their values (#2847, fixes #2840).
  • flatten_keys() on a lazy stack keeps each member's values and shares their tensors; before, every member got the first member's UnbatchedTensor, and leaves were copies (#2890, fixes #2869).

Non-tensor data and UnbatchedTensor

  • NonTensorData.update_at_ with a NumPy array index raises the RuntimeError that a list or tensor index raises; before, it raised a confusing ValueError (#2727).
  • Writing non-tensor data at a 0-d True or None index works on a tensordict without batch dims; before, it raised IndexError (#2750).
  • set of an UnbatchedTensor into a lazy stack stores it in every member, and flatten_keys() and unflatten_keys() work on such stacks; before, these raised (#2867, fixes #2864).
  • update_ and copy_ of an UnbatchedTensor in a lazy stack work along any stack dim; before, a stack dim other than 0 raised ValueError (#2873, fixes #2868).

Tensorclasses

  • A tensorclass's get_at takes default= and passes other keywords, such as as_list=True, to get, as TensorDict.get_at does; before, it raised KeyError: 'default' (#2832, fixes #2830).

TypedTensorDict

  • In-place math on a TypedTensorDict over lazy stacks whose members hold different keys works; before, it raised or wrote entries it should not (#2760, #2769, #2839, fixes #2739, fixes #2759).
  • dense.copy_(src) and dense.update_(src) write the nested entries of a TypedTensorDict over a lazy stack; before, those entries kept their old values (#2770, fixes #2768).
  • t + 1, copy_ and update_ work on a TypedTensorDict over a lazy stack, whatever its members; before, they raised or skipped nested entries (#2774, fixes #2771, fixes #2772, fixes #2773).

detail.body:
Updates the requirements on [tensordict](https://github.com/pytorch/tensordict) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from tensordict's releases.

TensorDict v0.15.1

Highlights

TensorDict 0.15.1 is a patch release with 46 bug fixes. They cover update_, copy_ and in-place math on lazy stacks, h5 files and TypedTensorDict, UnbatchedTensor and non-tensor data, NumPy conversion, tensordict.nn, and torch.compile. There are no new features or deprecations. Several fixes change behavior that was previously wrong; see "Behavior changes" below.

Bug Fixes

Construction and conversion

  • td.new_tensor(data) takes a list, tuple, NumPy array or scalar, as torch.Tensor.new_tensor does; before, it raised AttributeError (#2748, fixes #2747).
  • A list of tensors of different shapes in TensorDict(...) or set becomes a NonTensorStack, as with from_dict; before, it raised AttributeError (#2751).
  • NumPy arrays with negative strides, fields of packed structured arrays and big-endian arrays are copied into a tensordict; before, they raised a misleading ValueError (#2853, #2855, fixes #2852, fixes #2854).

Keys, get, set and update

  • td.update({"x": td}), and p["x"] = p on a TensorDictParams, raise ValueError; before, they left a tensordict that holds itself, or raised RecursionError (#2764).
  • Gradients flow through update_ and copy_; before, backward() through the written leaves raised, and compiled code with these calls failed to compile (#2881, fixes #2863, fixes #2886).
  • copy_, update_ (also with keys_to_update) and in-place math write the h5 files and lazy stacks that a TensorDict holds; before, these silently kept their values (#2777, #2838, fixes #2775, fixes #2780).
  • split_keys(..., reproduce_struct=True) puts each non-tensor entry, and each entry that only some lazy-stack members hold, in one part; before, every part got a copy (#2802, #2841, fixes #2782, fixes #2803).

Arithmetic, reductions and torch functions

  • torch.where(mask, 0, td) and torch.where(mask, tensor, td) work on tensordicts and tensorclasses; before, they raised AttributeError and TypeError (#2762, fixes #2743).
  • named_apply(fn, out=buf) writes into buf and returns it, as apply does; before, it returned a new tensordict and left buf unchanged (#2846, fixes #2845).

Lazy stacks, stack and cat

  • Printing a lazy stack or a TypedTensorDict over one stacks no tensors; before, it stacked every entry twice, which can exhaust GPU memory (#2799, #2829, fixes #2783, fixes #2800).
  • filter_empty_() and split_keys() work on a lazy stack whose members hold empty sub-tensordicts; before, they raised KeyError (#2806, fixes #2796).
  • When one member of a lazy stack rejects its part of update_ or copy_, nothing is written; before, the earlier members were already written (#2837, fixes #2776).
  • update_ and copy_ broadcast a 0-d or size-1 value into a lazy stack inside a TensorDict; before, the value was silently dropped (#2850, fixes #2834).
  • empty(recurse=True) drops the tensors of a lazy stack inside a tensordict, as at the root; before, member-only tensors kept their values (#2847, fixes #2840).
  • flatten_keys() on a lazy stack keeps each member's values and shares their tensors; before, every member got the first member's UnbatchedTensor, and leaves were copies (#2890, fixes #2869).

Non-tensor data and UnbatchedTensor

  • NonTensorData.update_at_ with a NumPy array index raises the RuntimeError that a list or tensor index raises; before, it raised a confusing ValueError (#2727).
  • Writing non-tensor data at a 0-d True or None index works on a tensordict without batch dims; before, it raised IndexError (#2750).
  • set of an UnbatchedTensor into a lazy stack stores it in every member, and flatten_keys() and unflatten_keys() work on such stacks; before, these raised (#2867, fixes #2864).
  • update_ and copy_ of an UnbatchedTensor in a lazy stack work along any stack dim; before, a stack dim other than 0 raised ValueError (#2873, fixes #2868).

Tensorclasses

  • A tensorclass's get_at takes default= and passes other keywords, such as as_list=True, to get, as TensorDict.get_at does; before, it raised KeyError: 'default' (#2832, fixes #2830).

TypedTensorDict

  • In-place math on a TypedTensorDict over lazy stacks whose members hold different keys works; before, it raised or wrote entries it should not (#2760, #2769, #2839, fixes #2739, fixes #2759).
  • dense.copy_(src) and dense.update_(src) write the nested entries of a TypedTensorDict over a lazy stack; before, those entries kept their old values (#2770, fixes #2768).
  • t + 1, copy_ and update_ work on a TypedTensorDict over a lazy stack, whatever its members; before, they raised or skipped nested entries (#2774, fixes #2771, fixes #2772, fixes #2773).

... (truncated)
